> 
> The death is admission, not a timeout or drain rate. Code reads are synchronous client calls (FOREVER, no busy retry): FILE_WAIT_US never applies. erofsd and walfsd cap Files at 32 per (account, label set), the R26 share is max(1, 32/(holders+1)), and every connection holds its root fid for life (Tattach charges it). At 16 connections of one account at the system volume (13 leases + 2 sessions + 1) no connection of hers can walk anything: every module load of every VM refused `too many open files`. The shell's hub keeps root+cwd at walfsd, so it loses its working fid there from the 8th lease (emfile). Where the refusal lands decides the death: /project attach -> exit 14 (seen, rv32 2 harts, agents 13 and 14); boot-pack or first start-module read -> the VM parks silently for ever; the start module's second read in vm.spawn -> exit 1 (STEWARD9's agent-36, explained not reproduced); a lazy load -> undef; the input read -> Echo spins.
> 
> Rates, one hart, both widths alike: launch 1.3-1.9 s at 1-4 leases, 4-6.7 s at 13-14 (rv32 two harts 3.1 -> 11.5 s); start-up 35-140 s beside 3-11 others; loads 30-85 KB/s per agent; a 2 KB write to /project 8-29 s, etimedout twice; verityd holds ~10 %. The pages/requests term is not on this path. Supported today: 13 leases of one account; 7 before the shell's hub loses at the data volume.
> 
> Decisions (section 5): the Files cap/share rule against the connection count (derive from the manifests as state is; root fid out of the share; floor at two); what a refused code read does (retry refusals in the sync client; a VM that cannot start exits with a code, not parks); the data volume's writes as a finding of its own; the count and rates to state; phase 2's case. No fix committed.

The one condition: confirm from the hub's code that at erofsd:system a connection holds at most one working fid at once (it should — no cwd, serial opens); if a real path holds two, that makes w = 2 the need there, not margin, and you set it so with the reason. At walfsd w = 2 is right because the hub keeps its cwd beside a working fid — the measured need, not margin.
